title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Casablanca and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape and Valle de Casablanca, often with Costa, the coastal descriptor added in 2011. Casablanca is part of the larger Aconcagua region. Chile's 85% rules apply. Many large Chilean wineries have Casablanca vineyards for their whites.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc suits Chilean seafood: ceviche, machas, razor clams, congrio, conger eel, and goat's cheese and salads. Chardonnay suits crab, chicken and creamy fish; Pinot Noir suits salmon and duck. Serve whites at 7 to 10 degrees, Pinot at 14 to 15.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc?
steps.explanation: Citrus and acidity match the lime-cured fish.

steps.body: Valparaíso, near Casablanca, is famous for seafood, a natural pairing with the valley's crisp whites.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show Valle de Casablanca and often Costa
Sauvignon Blanc suits ceviche and seafood
